classification.difficultyReason: Choose the arc opposite the requested vertex, sometimes finding a reflex central angle first; other parts require equal-radius isosceles angles before applying the centre-to-circumference relationship.

spec.description: Circle with A left, B above and C upper-right, chords AB and BC, radii OA and OC, and 160 degrees in the upper central sector.
spec.mathematics: The central sector containing B is 160 degrees. Angle ABC subtends the opposite 200-degree arc AC.
spec.answerVisibility: 160 degrees is a given; the 100-degree answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^\circ-160^\circ\\&=200^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{200^\circ}{2}\\&=100^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Use the central angle standing on the same arc $AC$ as $\angle ABC$.

spec.description: Circle with A above, B right and C below, chords AB and BC, centre O and two nearly opposite radii.
spec.mathematics: The right central sector AOC containing B is 171 degrees. OA and OC do not form a diameter.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^\circ-171^\circ\\&=189^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{189^\circ}{2}\\&=94.5^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Use the central angle standing on the same arc $AC$ as $\angle ABC$.

spec.description: Circle with quadrilateral ABCD, radii OA and OC and an 80-degree given inside angle ADC.
spec.mathematics: Angle ADC subtends the 160-degree arc AC containing B. Angle ABC subtends the complementary 200-degree arc. OA and OC are not a diameter.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=2\times80^\circ\\&=160^\circ\\\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^\circ-160^\circ\\&=200^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{200^\circ}{2}\\&=100^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Each central angle is twice the circumference angle standing on its arc.

spec.description: Circle with quadrilateral DCBA, centre O, radii OC and OA, and the 61-degree given at D.
spec.mathematics: Angle CDA is 61 degrees. B lies on the 122-degree minor arc CA, so angle ABC stands on the 238-degree major arc CA.
spec.answerVisibility: 61 degrees is a given; the answer is hidden.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=2\times61^\circ\\&=122^\circ\\\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^\circ-122^\circ\\&=238^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{238^\circ}{2}\\&=119^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Each central angle is twice the circumference angle standing on its arc.

spec.description: Circle with triangle ABC and radii OA, OB and OC. A leader from the left-hand 20-degree label points between CA and CO at C.
spec.mathematics: OA equals OC, so triangle AOC has equal base angles of 20 degrees and central angle 140 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given angle ACO is labelled.

answer.worked:
$OA=OC$ (radii), so $\angle OAC=\angle ACO=20^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=180^\circ-20^\circ-20^\circ\\&=140^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{140^\circ}{2}\\&=70^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on arc $AC$.

spec.description: Circle with triangle ABC and radii OA, OB and OC. The outside upper-right 24-degree label has a leader pointing between AO and AC at A.
spec.mathematics: OA equals OC, so triangle AOC has equal base angles of 24 degrees and central angle 132 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given angle OAC is labelled.

answer.worked:
$OA=OC$ (radii), so $\angle ACO=\angle OAC=24^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=180^\circ-24^\circ-24^\circ\\&=132^\circ\\\angle ABC&=\frac{132^\circ}{2}\\&=66^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on arc $AC$.
